response.justification: The candidate is an experienced senior/staff full-stack software engineer with a strong web, backend, and testing background, but the role requires deep hardware-domain expertise — SoC and IP modeling, AI accelerator architecture, deep-learning workload performance analysis, and hardware-software co-design — none of which appear in the resume. The only adjacent signals are brief C/C++ work at National Instruments (2014-2015), low-latency backend services in D, and a wave-field-synthesis audio thesis; these do not approach principal-level hardware architecture. Education (BS in CS, 2012) with ~14 years of experience meets the formal bar, but the experience is in an unrelated domain, so there is no credible path to being productive as a Principal Performance Architect.
strengths: 14+ years of engineering experience across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded
Demonstrated low-latency, high-throughput systems work (millions of req/s in D)
Strong engineering rigor: TDD, CI/CD, open-source tooling, teaching and public talks
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, RTL, or hardware architecture experience
No AI/deep-learning workload, GPU, SIMD/MIMD, or accelerator optimization background
Recent work is TypeScript/Node product engineering, far from systems/hardware co-design

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture expertise
No AI accelerator / DNN workload optimization experience
Seniority and breadth of general software engineering experience
